The search for "EditorConfig specification" returned the following summary:
The **EditorConfig specification** defines a simple file format and collection of text formatting rules used to maintain consistent coding styles for multiple developers working on the same project across various text editors and IDEs[1][2]. 

The official specification is maintained at [spec.editorconfig.org](https://spec.editorconfig.org/)[3]. Below is a breakdown of how the specification works, its file structure, syntax, and standard properties.

---

### 1. File Format Basics (`.editorconfig`)
* **Filename:** Configuration files are always named `.editorconfig`[4][1] and placed inside project directories[1].
* **Encoding:** Config files must be encoded in **UTF-8** (with or without a Byte Order Mark), using either `CRLF` or `LF` line separators[5].
* **Syntax Structure:** The format is heavily inspired by INI files[1][6]:
  * **Blank lines** and white space-only lines are ignored[1][6].
  * **Comments** start with a number sign (`#`) or a semicolon (`;`) at the beginning of a line[1][6]. 
  * **Section headers** are enclosed in square brackets (`[...]`) and contain glob patterns matching file paths[1][6].
  * **Key-value pairs** use an equal sign (`=`) to assign formatting properties (e.g., `indent_size = 4`)[7][6].

---

### 2. Root Property
At the very top of a `.editorconfig` file, you can designate whether it is the root configuration file for the project:
```ini
root = true
```
* When `root = true`, EditorConfig core parsers will stop looking for other `.editorconfig` files in parent directories[4]. If omitted or set to `false`, it continues searching up the directory tree[4].

---

### 3. Glob Patterns (Section Headers)
Section headers dictate which files the subsequent rules apply to[1][6]. Patterns are relative to the directory where the `.editorconfig` file resides[6]:

* `*` : Matches any string of characters, excluding path separators (`/`)
* `**` : Matches any string of characters, including path separators
* `?` : Matches any single character
* `[name]` : Matches any single character in the set (`name`)
* `[!name]` : Matches any single character not in the set (`name`)
* `{s1,s2,s3}` : Matches any of the given strings separated by commas (brace expansion)[4]

**Examples:**
* `[*]` — Matches all files[4][6]
* `[*.{js,py}]` — Matches all JavaScript and Python files[4]
* `[lib/**.js]` — Matches any JavaScript file inside the `lib` directory or its subdirectories[4]

---

### 4. Standard Properties
EditorConfig defines a core set of standard properties for text editing[5][6]:

| Property | Values | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `indent_style` | `space`, `tab` | Controls whether indentation uses spaces or tabs. |
| `indent_size` | Whole number | Specifies the number of columns used for each indentation level (often maps to spaces). |
| `tab_width` | Whole number | Width of a tab character (defaults to `indent_size` value if not specified). |
| `end_of_line` | `lf`, `cr`, `crlf` | Line break style (`lf` for Unix/macOS, `crlf` for Windows)[4]. |
| `charset` | `latin1`, `utf-8`, `utf-8-bom`, `utf-16be`, `utf-16le` | File character encoding[4]. |
| `trim_trailing_whitespace` | `true`, `false` | Automatically removes any whitespace characters preceding a newline character at the end of lines. |
| `insert_final_newline` | `true`, `false` | Ensures files end with a newline character when saved[4]. |

*(Note: Many tools and extensions also support language-specific extensions or custom properties like those used for .NET code style analysis[8]).*

---

### 5. Order of Precedence
When multiple `.editorconfig` files or rules overlap, EditorConfig resolves them using two major rules[6]:

1. **Hierarchical Precedence (Directory-based):** 
   Files closer to the target file being edited override rules defined in `.editorconfig` files higher up in the directory tree[5][6].
2. **Top-to-Bottom Precedence (File-based):** 
   Within a single `.editorconfig` file, rules are read from top to bottom[5][6]. If a file matches multiple sections, **the later (lower) matching rules override the earlier ones**[5][6].

#### Example File Layout:
```ini
# root configuration
root = true

# 1. Broad global defaults
[*]
indent_style = space
indent_size = 4
end_of_line = lf
insert_final_newline = true

# 2. Override specifically for Python files further down
[*.py]
indent_size = 4

# 3. Override for Makefiles to use hard tabs instead of spaces
[Makefile]
indent_style = tab
```
